cue: How do you say something is hopeless to look for?

es.text: Buscar una aguja en un pajar
es.literal: to look for a needle in a haystack
es.meaning: To search for something almost impossible to find.
es.example: Encontrar ese archivo sin la fecha es buscar una aguja en un pajar.
es.exampleTranslation: Finding that file without the date is looking for a needle in a haystack.

it.literal: to look for a needle in the haystack
it.meaning: To search for something almost impossible to find.
it.example: Trovare quel file senza la data è come cercare un ago nel pagliaio.
it.exampleTranslation: Finding that file without the date is like looking for a needle in a haystack.

bridge.note: Word for word the same hopeless search, and one article between them. Spanish looks in A haystack — en UN pajar, any haystack, one of many. Italian looks in THE haystack — nel pagliaio, definite, as though the haystack were already agreed on. Nothing in the meaning turns on it, which is exactly why it slips past: there is no logic to derive it from, only the habit of the language.

interference.es_to_it: Italian contracts the preposition and the article into one word: NEL pagliaio. 'In un pagliaio' is grammatical and is not the idiom. Italian also usually introduces the whole thing with come — è come cercare un ago nel pagliaio.
interference.it_to_es: Spanish keeps them apart and indefinite: EN UN pajar. 'En el pajar' points at a specific haystack and breaks the image.
